help.tips[0].examples[1].en: the solution of the problem by the experts
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: The subject of the verb becomes a genitive attribute: der Vorstand → des Vorstands.
help.tips[0].en.text: Die Regierung entscheidet → die Entscheidung der Regierung / ihre Entscheidung. Man senkt die Steuern → die Senkung der Steuern / die Steuersenkung. Man untersucht das Problem → die Untersuchung des Problems. Sie einigen sich auf einen Plan → die Einigung auf einen Plan.
help.tips[0].en.title: Subject → genitive or possessive; object → genitive, compound or preposition
help.tips[0].en.trap: two genitives in a row (die Untersuchung der Wirkung des Medikaments) are correct but heavy; good style replaces one with a compound or a preposition (die Wirkungsuntersuchung des Medikaments; die Untersuchung zur Wirkung).
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: After the successful completion of the project by the team, the evaluation followed.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: When the minister arrived, the meeting began. → On the minister's arrival the meeting began.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: The adverb becomes an adjective and takes the ending after die in the nominative singular: die gründliche Prüfung.
help.tips[1].en.text: schnell entscheiden → die schnelle Entscheidung · von Experten gelöst → die Lösung durch Experten · als er ankam → bei seiner Ankunft · nachdem sie abgereist war → nach ihrer Abreise. Everything a clause carried finds a slot in the noun phrase.
help.tips[1].en.title: Adverb → adjective; agent → durch / von; time → bei / nach / vor
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: the commission's proposal to amend the law
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: Prices have risen sharply. → the sharp rise in prices
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: ankommen has its own noun, die Ankunft; Ankommung doesn't exist, and das Ankommen is neuter, so it can't follow die.
help.tips[2].en.text: entscheiden → Entscheidung · lösen → Lösung · ankommen → Ankunft · abfahren → Abfahrt · verlieren → Verlust · wachsen → Wachstum · vorschlagen → Vorschlag · ergeben → Ergebnis · erkennen → Erkenntnis · informieren → Information. Check the noun exists; if not, the capitalised infinitive always does (das Warten).
help.tips[2].en.title: Which noun? -ung, stem, -e, Infinitiv, -nis
help.tips[3].examples[0].en: Because the company reacted quickly, the damage stayed small.
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: After the contracts had been signed, construction began. → After the signing of the contracts construction began.
help.tips[3].check.whyEn: The conjunction obwohl becomes the preposition trotz + genitive; wegen would turn the concession into a cause.
help.tips[3].en.text: 1 verb → noun · 2 subject → genitive/possessive · 3 object → genitive/compound/preposition · 4 adverb → adjective · 5 conjunction → preposition (weil → wegen, nachdem → nach). Run them in order and any sentence folds.
help.tips[3].en.title: Clause → phrase: five moves
help.context.en: The university's decision to introduce a new degree programme led to a change in the examination regulations. After the institute's investigation of demand and the evaluation of the results, the faculties agreed on a joint proposal. The arrival of the first students is planned for autumn – despite the loss of two professorships.
help.mistakes[0].whyEn: The subject becomes a genitive attribute.
help.mistakes[1].whyEn: The agent of a nominalised action takes durch.
help.hookEn: Fold a whole clause into one dense noun phrase, the way reports and official letters do, and unfold it again when you read.
help.introEn: You already know the six ways to make a noun from a verb; now you use them to rewrite whole sentences. Nominalisation turns a clause into a noun phrase: 'Die Regierung entschied, die Steuern zu senken' → 'die Entscheidung der Regierung, die Steuern zu senken' / 'die Entscheidung der Regierung zur Steuersenkung'. The subject becomes a genitive attribute (der Regierung) or a possessive (ihre Entscheidung); the object becomes a genitive (die Senkung der Steuern), a compound (Steuersenkung) or a prepositional attribute (die Entscheidung über …); adverbs become adjectives (schnell entscheiden → die schnelle Entscheidung); the verb's preposition stays (sich einigen auf → die Einigung auf). The result is the Nominalstil of academic and administrative German — dense, verb-poor, noun-heavy — which you must read fluently and write in moderation. Reports, official letters and any text that summarises a graph are written in it.
help.rememberEn[0]: Verb → noun; subject → genitive; object → genitive / compound / preposition; adverb → adjective; conjunction → preposition.
help.rememberEn[1]: Avoid genitive chains: compound or preposition instead.
help.recallEn.known: From "Nominalisierung: die sechs Typen": verb → noun, and the gender each type takes.
help.recallEn.today: Turning a whole clause into one noun phrase: subject, object, adverb and time all change.
sentences[1].whyEn: reagieren → die Reaktion — -ieren verbs often take -ion.
sentences[3].whyEn: lösen + -ung: die Lösung; the doer becomes durch + accusative.
sentences[5].whyEn: untersuchen + -ung: die Untersuchung; the object becomes genitive.
sentences[6].whyEn: vorschlagen → der Vorschlag — the stem as a noun, masculine.
sentences[8].whyEn: verlieren → der Verlust; zweier is zwei's genitive.
sentences[9].whyEn: sich einigen + -ung: die Einigung — the auf survives.
sentences[10].whyEn: protestieren → der Protest; trotz demands the genitive: des Protests.
sentences[12].whyEn: abfliegen → der Abflug — the bare stem.
sentences[13].whyEn: steigen → der Anstieg — bei + dative: beim Anstieg.
